BackendTests replays backend-matrix.json's client rows.

config.resolve.note: Member names compare by scalar value, but JSONValue keeps the first of two canonically equivalent names (WIRE-CONTRACT-V3 §10).

config.mirror.note: The Swift mirror is rendered by tools/gen-mirrors.ts.

config.local.note: config.set, clear and clearAll persist through a LocalConfigStore (UserDefaults by default), validate against the catalog and raise client.events .config; config.setting(key) returns a handle whose current() gives the effective value, its source and lock, and onConfigChange(key | "*", listener) returns a cancellable ConfigSubscription (configChanges(key) is the AsyncStream form), fed by the same change observation as client.events for local writes and syncs (LocalConfigTests).

config.sync.note: config.set, clear and setting(key).sync() route through the Cloud Sync machine while a person is signed in (SyncPort over CloudSyncHost, PolarisKey/CloudSyncApi.swift); setting(key).sync() reports the setting's sync state and changes carry an origin, local or remote (CloudSyncSettingsTests).

devices.attest.note: client.devices.attest() (PolarisKey/DevicesClient.swift): POST devices/attest/challenge, DCAppAttestService.attestKey over SHA-256(UTF-8(requestHash)) through PolarisKeyPlatform's AppAttestClient, POST devices/attest; the key id kept in the Keychain (account app_attest_key) and re-attested with a fresh key when a reinstall, migration or restore killed it. Registered as Core's attestor so a 403 attestation_required edge-mint or commerce claim attests once and retries once. Unsupported runtime on macOS and where App Attest does not run (the simulator); outlet on an iOS build with an embedded provisioning profile.

identity.oidc.note: Native browser sign-in (loopback, scheme, claimed HTTPS) waits on I-15; the host-supplied https redirect is identity.redirect.web. The device-code route is client.identity.signIn.start(SignInOptions(browser:)), which opens the device-code verification URL in ASWebAuthenticationSession; session.wait() polls /identity/auth/device/poll (identity.devicecode; the old /identity/auth/poll is retired and the Worker no longer serves it).

identity.devicelabel.note: PX-W13: normalizeDeviceLabel over Unicode scalars, CoreOptions.deviceName and the platform default (macOS Host.current().localizedName, iOS-family UIDevice.current.name), on signIn.start, activation and registration; SignInPrompt.deviceName is the Worker's echo. PolarisKeyUI has no device-code sign-in view to show it in (ui.kit is planned and unowned).

identity.redirect.web.note: signIn.start(SignInOptions(channel: .redirect, redirectUri:)) builds the S256 authorize URL from discovery (IdentityRedirect, CryptoKit) for a browser the host opens; session.complete(callbackUrl:) checks the redirect URI, state and iss before anything is sent, then redeems the code at discovery's token endpoint. Single use; a refusal is a typed SignInError and never wipes the token. Loopback, scheme and claimed-HTTPS redirects are I-15's; the licence choice (license_choice=app) is identity.choice.

identity.choice.note: SignInOptions(licenseChoice: .app) sends license_choice=app (only when discovery lists the four choice routes; else the card chooses) and session.complete(callbackUrl:) then settles .chooseLicense(PendingSignIn); identity.choice.licenses/devices/complete/cancel(grant:) take the grant (complete with keep also sends the device's own bearer, which the Worker reads as held; every other choice sends none), store the device token on complete like a sign-in, and throw a typed ChoiceError (invalid_grant, license_choice_required and device_limit with a fresh view, not_found, rate_limited with retryAfterSeconds); UnsupportedError(product) when a route is not published. LicenseChoiceModel (PolarisKeyUICore, @Observable) drives the LicenseChoice screen's KitInputs from the SDK.

identity.devicecode.choice.note: signIn.start(SignInOptions(licenseChoice: .app, ...)) sends loginHint, nameHint, purpose and licenseChoice on the device start (the hints always; licenseChoice app only when discovery carries deviceChoice and the four choice routes); a poll status choose settles session.wait() as .chooseLicense(PendingSignIn), the redirect's outcome, which identity.choice completes. A choose that was not asked for is a sign-in-failed.

identity.keyreturn.note: LK-SKIP.9: the opt-in, the via rule and the activated outcome, with the replayer.

identity.redirect.native.note: I-15b.4: signIn.start(SignInOptions(channel: .redirect)) with no redirectUri (NativeRedirect.swift, NativeSignIn.swift, NativeBrowser.swift; the client-core redirect.ts helpers ported). macOS: an NWListener bound to 127.0.0.1 on an OS-assigned port before the request is pushed, the default browser (NSWorkspace), one 303 to the customer host's return page, then closed. iOS and visionOS: ASWebAuthenticationSession with the registered scheme (read from Info.plist, or SignInOptions.native) or a claimed HTTPS link (17.4 and later), not ephemeral; a scheme or claimed delivery from elsewhere goes to signIn.handleRedirect(url). The code is redeemed from the pushing device with the PKCE verifier; headless hosts (D-68), a product that serves no request endpoint and a sandbox that cannot bind throw redirect-unavailable when no scheme or claimed class applies. The redirect-native-* and locker-redirect-native transcripts replay in TranscriptTests; NativeRedirectTests maps each listener rule over a real socket. A simulator or device check is still owed for ASWebAuthenticationSession.

identity.exchange.note: identity.exchange(kind:subjectToken:nonce:) and exchangeNonce(kind:) (PolarisKeyIdentity): the nonce route registers the device keys, the token route takes the pkey-proof/1 exchange proof over nonce.key and the token hash; the outcome is signedIn, confirm (PendingConsent, completed through identity.choice.complete(grant:choice:consent:)), choose, needsSignIn or unavailable, and refusals are a typed ExchangeError. A 404 on either route, a discovery with no exchange member or a memory-only key port is unavailable with no request. Replayed against the exchange-* transcripts (TranscriptTests). Sign in with Apple itself is I-44.4.

identity.gamecenter.note: PolarisKeyGameCenter (I-44.5, standalone): GameCenterIdentity checks the local player is signed in (authenticateHandler, never presenting Game Center's view) and scopedIDsArePersistent(), takes fetchItemsForIdentityVerificationSignature() and encodes the gc1. token (GameCenterToken, V5 §12.11.7) over a GameCenterPlayerPort; ExchangeKind.gamecenter sends subject_token_type urn:polaris-key:token-type:gamecenter-signature; GameCenterSignInProvider (opt-in product PolarisKeyGameCenterSignIn; the umbrella links no GameKit) is the autoSignIn provider. Replayed against exchange-gamecenter-* (TranscriptTests) with a fake player; link-game waits on identity.link. The signature hash and timestamp unit are unconfirmed on a real device (owner step).

identity.pgs.note: Play Games runs only on Android.

identity.autosignin.note: autoSignIn() rungs 1-4 (plan-auto-sign-in §1, I-44): a stored sign-in, then the platform provider's silent mode where it has one (Apple has none; Game Center is I-44.5), then its one sheet under prompt: .optional; every refusal is a result.

identity.restore.note: Rung 2 of autoSignIn() (PolarisKeyIdentity/Restore.swift): the restore grant over the PlatformBackupStore item (the umbrella's RestoreBackup.swift adapter), enrolment after every completed sign-in and once a day on rung 1, sign-out deletion (DELETE restore queued for the next launch, the synchronizable item, the signed-out flag), AutoSignInOptions.restore and backupAccessGroup (I-49.9). The restore-* transcripts and discovery-identity-restore are replayed (I-49.10).

identity.nearby.note: Nearby sign-in, both devices (I-44.12, I-44.13). The LAN half is CC-15 (client.cloudConnect.nearby.request and onRequest). D: identity.signIn.startNearby (NearbySignInSession: approvers, choose, code, wait, confirmAccount, declineAccount, wrap) over nearby/start and nearby/poll, with the unconfirmed mark and the KEYRING_WRAP opened through the key ring (SyncKeyring.adoptWrap) only after the confirmation. The kit: NearbyApprovalModel bound to the SDK, the account menu's Approve a nearby device row in PolarisKeySettings, the licence choice and the waiting screen; the nearby-* transcripts are replayed for D's start and poll steps and M's approve steps. A runtime without the Network framework answers nearby-unsupported; the real-device run is owed (OS-6).

release.fetch.note: client.update.fetch(version:buildId:size:sha256:to:) (PolarisKeyUpdate/Install.swift) streams through the client's transport (PolarisTransport.stream) into <to>.part, resumes with Range and If-Range on the payload SHA-256 (206 appends after re-hashing the part, 200 restarts, 416 verifies), maps a refusal to the body's registered wire code, and verifies size and SHA-256 before the file appears at <to>; the replayer runs all three steps of release-fetch-gated.json.

update.feeds.note: client.update.feedUrl(_:channel:velopackChannel:buildId:) over updateFeedURL (PolarisKeyUpdate/Install.swift); FeedUrlMatrixTests drives every feed-url-matrix.json row.

update.content.note: PolarisKeyCore's feedContent, holdsOf (stampHolds) and decideUpdate with UpdateContentInput (selectPackRows, the composition, prestage, contentBlock, packs; bootDecision gives required only for revoked required content); runUpdateCheck runs P4-13 §2.5 steps 10–14. update.driver.note: Sparkle on macOS: PolarisSparkle.start(client:channel:bundle:userDriver:) (PolarisKeyUpdate), and PolarisSparkleUserDriver (PolarisKeyUpdateUI, UK-08.6), the SwiftUI SPUUserDriver and its one update window; SparkleUserDriverTests and SparkleUserDriverMappingTests (the mapping table, every reply once, no invented percentage, nothing after an error).

update.bootguard.note: PolarisKeyCore AppBootGuard (client.bootGuard, client.markBootAttempt/confirmBoot with PolarisKeyUpdate): bootGuardAction over a launch counter kept beside the credential (Store record boot-guard); an Apple app has no previous build to roll back to, so after MAX_FAILED_BOOTS it journals P6-03 boot_rolled_back (code no-previous) once and answers rollBackUnavailable; the first confirmed launch of a new build journals update_confirmed. client.boot() marks the attempt and confirms BOOT_OK_SECONDS after ready.

packs.revoke.note: PolarisKeyCore's revocationOf, verifyRevocation and newerRevocation (every revocationCases vector); PackEngine keeps the sibling revocations.json (revocationsStored in state.json first, never created empty, re-verified per entry on load, relearn, the 256-target cap, torn and unreadable rules, recoverState clears relearn) and refuses revoked releases with pack-revoked (detail relearn for a refused baseline it cannot fetch).

packs.delegation.note: PolarisKeyCore verifyReleaseRecord (the delegated path, steps 13 and 16), verifyDelegation, recordRevoked and PolarisKeyPacks dataOnlyRefusal; the PackEngine fetches and caches delegations, refuses non-data-only delegated installs with pack-not-data-only, stores PackInstall.delegation and refuses releases under a revoked delegation (pack-revoked, detail delegation); DelegationConformanceTests drives every delegationCases and dataOnlyCases vector.

packs.plan.note: PolarisKeyPacks' plan, selectVariant and planTarget; every plan-matrix.json row, variant case and target case in PlanMatrixTests.

packs.index.files.note: PolarisKeyPacks' parseFilesIndex, checkPaths and treeDigest; filesIndexCases in ContentConformanceTests, read from the checkout.

packs.index.chunks.note: PolarisKeyPacks' parseChunkIndex and parseChunkIndexBytes (u64 from two little-endian u32 reads composed byte by byte, saturated at 2^53); chunkIndexCases in ContentConformanceTests under both libzstd paths.

packs.apply.full.note: applyFull, streamed through libzstd's ZSTD_decompressStream (and one-shot without it); applyCases under both paths.

packs.apply.file.note: applyFile with the type-neutral container rebuild; applyCases under both paths.

Without StoreKit purchase/restore answer the typed runtime N/A.

sync.scenarios.note: The machine (PolarisKeyCore/Sync/CloudSyncMachine*.swift) runs conformance/corpus/v2/sync-scenarios.json through SyncScenariosTests and CloudSyncMachineTests, with the host codec cases in HostCodecTests.

sync.settings.note: client.cloudSync: status(), flush(), newRecoveryCode() and recoveryCode, and the cloudSync case of client.events. CloudSyncHost (PolarisKey/CloudSyncHost.swift) owns one machine, the transport (no redirect, 8 MiB cap, 15 s), the state file and the sign-out chain (flush, machine sign-out, key ring forget, purge; a ring that cannot forget stops the sign-out and keeps the data). Cloud Sync is off on Linux (FoundationNetworking). The cloudsync-* transcripts replay in TranscriptTests; CloudSyncHostTests, CloudSyncHostBoundsTests, CloudSyncHostFixesTests and CloudSyncSettingsTests.

sync.saves.note: client.cloudSync.saves (PolarisKey/CloudSyncSaves.swift, CloudSyncSavesBinding.swift): list(), read(_:options:), write(_:bytes:metadata:options:) (and write(_:source:...) and write(_:bytes:encoding:...)), resolve(_:keep:bytes:options:), delete(_:baseVersion:), revisions(_:), and client.cloudSync.transfers() with pause(), resume() and cancel() on each SaveTransfer. The machine holds the saves collection (file pointers, records(), putAt/removeAt with journal-only tickets, one outcome per ticket); the file goes first and the metadata `set` second on the version finalize answered, so no save is torn; in end-to-end mode the sealed metadata carries the $file binding and a read downloads the revision it names (a miss is sync-file-invalid); newerFormat from SavesOptions.saveFormatVersion; the 16-slot cap, conflicts as SaveConflict with keep local/remote/both, and transferProgress/transferDone/transferFailed on client.events (a cancelled write is a transferDone with state cancelled). The wait for the metadata write has no timeout: cancel(), a sign-out (the write is dropped) and the host's retries end it; a pause never does. The key ring's fileCodec(collection:) refuses with sync-locked on every call and stream piece once the ring locks. Sign-out and forget: lock the ring, purge the saves (journal, the person's chunk cache, waiting writes), then remove the root and the pin. CloudSyncSavesTests, CloudSyncSavesHostTests, ForgetOrderTests, SyncKeyringTests, SyncScenariosTests (fileRecordCases) and the cloudsync-files-single transcript.

sync.keyring.note: client.keyring (PolarisKey/SyncKeyring.swift, over PolarisKeyCore/Sync: CryptoKit HKDF, AES.GCM and HMAC, RFC 9180 mode_base written out over DeviceKeyPort.dh for open and an ephemeral Curve25519 key for seal): create(), unlock() (opens this device's wrap through the port's dh, so the agreement key never leaves the store), wrapTo()/removeWrap(), setRecoveryCode()/recover(), reset()/adopt()/openAdopted(), acceptRingChange(confirmed:), attach(_:) feeding setRoot, and the codec. The first root pins {ringId, epoch, rootKid} per product in the Core store; a served ring that differs is ringChanged and is never opened. The root is also kept in one Keychain item (sync-root, AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly, never synchronizable) that is used only while it matches the pin; forget() drops the root and the pin and runs from the release hook (a Keychain delete that fails stops the sign-out). Every type holding key material prints as redacted. SyncVectorsTests (hkdf, envelope, blind, canonicalJson, hpkeAnchor, wrap, recovery and adopt cases, plus an HPKE.Sender cross-check), SyncKeyringTests and the keyring-* transcripts in TranscriptTests.

sync.records.note: client.cloudSync.collection(_:) (PolarisKey/CloudSyncCollection.swift, async) returns a CloudSyncCollection over the host's machine: get, ids, put (ifVersion: .version(n) or .any, a compare-and-set whose outcome reaches on(_:) as .outcome), update(_:set:remove:), add, remove, delete(_:ifVersion:) and on(_:), whose CollectionSubscription.cancel() removes the listener. Refusals are returned as CollectionResult.refused, never thrown, with nothing sent: collection_unknown, op_invalid_for_policy, value_invalid (a union element over 1 KiB of canonical JSON, a merge field name empty or over 1 KiB, an empty id) and signed_out. The host builds the machine's collections from the catalog's cloudSync.collections (conflict, a template's conflict, conflictField; exact names and prefix.* patterns, the longest prefix winning) and keeps a handle's watches and outcome taps across a rebuild or purge. The machine adds update (one stamp over setField/removeField), delete (editedHlc except for union; revision uses removeAt), recordIds, watchRecords with `records` events, and tapOutcomes beside onOutcome. The host codec seals a merge field under k = id U+0000 field and a union element under k = id U+0000 canonicalJson(e), with blind("record"|"field"|"element"), and opens sealed fields and elements only when every envelope's k re-blinds to the names served. HostCodecCellsTests, CloudSyncCollectionTests, SyncScenariosTests, and the seven cloudsync-records-* transcripts in TranscriptTests.

sync.files.note: CloudSyncFileTransport (PolarisKey/CloudSyncFiles.swift) is the engine's FileTransport over the device bearer: a closed allow-list of the file routes (key charset, 64-hex chunk ids, no dot segments, only version=<digits> as a query), no redirect followed, JSON read to 1 MiB, error bodies to 64 KiB, a ranged GET to the range asked and a chunk to SYNC_CHUNK_MAX_STORED_BYTES, a deadline that grows with the body, Content-Digest on every PUT and Retry-After as seconds or a date capped at 3,600 before any integer conversion (a 503 unavailable from a down limiter backs off like a 429). CloudSyncFilesTests; the cloudsync-files-* transcripts replay in TranscriptTests (cloudsync-files-single also proves sync.saves and waits for it).

sync.files.delta.note: The chunks mode over the same transport (planChunks, putChunk, getChunk, the manifest through putSingle; the chunk-size cap is the generated SYNC_CHUNK_MAX_STORED_BYTES) and the S4 engine; a present chunk that became missing is sent again. The cloudsync-chunks and cloudsync-chunks-delta transcripts replay in TranscriptTests.

sync.transfer.background.note: CloudSyncBackground (PolarisKey/CloudSyncBackground.swift) behind CloudSyncOptions(backgroundTransfers: true): a background URLSession pkey.sync.<product> carrying each sealed part or chunk from a protected spool file, the bearer read per task and refreshed once on a 401, reconcile after a launch, and PolarisKeyClient.handleBackgroundEvents from the app delegate. An upload the system or a kill interrupted is reported once at saves start as transferFailed (transfer-failed) under saves:<id>; calling write again resumes it from the journal. Default off. CloudSyncBackgroundTests over a stubbed session port; the real session is proven on a device.

sync.e2e.note: Settings seal and open through the machine's E2E mode (CloudSyncOptions.encryption, default .e2e; app code only, never read from the Worker) over the key ring; guard (b) judges a conflict's server copy against the push's own cursor (X-1, the cursor is required). SyncScenariosTests replays every e2e scenario, e2e-conflict-plaintext-copy-refused included; SyncVectorsTests and HostCodecTests cover the vectors and the host codec.

connect.identity.note: client.connect (ConnectClient): identity() registers the device keys on first need (PUT devices/keys with the keys proof; a memory-only key store is invalid-options unless ConnectOptions.allowEphemeralKeys), fetches GET connect/identity, verifies the roster and certificate (PeerDocs, from peerCertCases, ringCases, peerAdmissionCases) against the effective trust set, binds them to this device and its keys, refuses a stale, foreign or unlisted roster, and keeps the roster, the certificate and K_disc in one Keychain item (connect-state, this-device-only, never synchronized; K_disc prints as redacted). Every fetch replaces K_disc; the previous key is kept for 24 hours from first seen and dropped when a device was lost or re-keyed. A held identity with more than 3.5 days of certificate is served without a request unless refresh. An unreadable record is store-failed and never overwritten. leave() (called first on sign-out and release, which fail closed) deletes the record; with none held it touches nothing. listDevices() reads connect/devices. Typed: account_required, device_keys_required and ring_too_large come back verbatim; the service off is the product N/A. The connect transcripts replay with the relay slice.

connect.noise.note: PolarisKeyCore PeerNoise: Noise_XX_25519_AESGCM_SHA256 over CryptoKit, a zero DH refusing with dh_zero; PeerNoiseTests replays noise-vectors.json.

connect.protocol.note: PolarisKeyCore peer codecs, frames, relay envelopes, SAS and the peer session (modes a, v, p; commit-reveal SAS, handshake limiter; HELLO display data cleaned: platform in [A-Za-z0-9 ._+-] up to 32 characters else Unknown, app cleaned like label, a HELLO in modes v and p up to 4 KiB, held host records up to 16 and 16 KiB), PeerLink, and the trust manager's accept-peer; PeerBytesTests, PeerCodecTests, PeerSessionTests, PeerSessionSASTests, ConnectSessionTests and TrustAcceptPeerTests replay peer-matrix.json.

connect.lan.note: PolarisKeyPlatform BonjourBrowse and BonjourPipes (Network.framework: NWBrowser, NWListener, NWConnection; the LAN address rule lanVerdict of V5 §15.4.1 (LanAddress.swift: IPv4, fe80::/10, fc00::/7 and an on-link global IPv6 address) judged on a host and port as text before connect and on the connected path's remote and local endpoints before the first byte, and on an accepted source before a slot and again before the host sees the pipe, a non-LAN accept closed with no read; the 30 s authentication bound; unauthenticated sockets capped per address 4, per group 16 (the link for fe80::/10, the /24 for IPv4, the /64 for ULA and global) and 32 in all, a link-local key with its zone; a browse hit is resolved with DNS-SD on the interface the browse reported and every address is judged by lanVerdict and the connected subnets of the interface it came back on (LanResolve.swift, BonjourResolve.swift) before any connect, the SRV port must be 1024 to 65535, a service endpoint is never handed to NWConnection, and the dial falls through to the next address after a failed handshake (wrong_peer ends it); the residual is that the address is resolver-returned, not source-equal; the accept gate looks up an own address on the receiving interface; PeerCodecTests runs every peer-matrix.json lanAddresses row, skips the candidates rows because Swift reads no CANDIDATES entry, and skips mdnsAnswers because the OS resolver owns it) and PolarisKey ConnectLan (advert rotation, browse index, dial, wrong_peer, session caps); the Info.plist needs NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription and the NSBonjourServices entry _pkeypeer._tcp, and a sandboxed macOS app needs com.apple.security.network.client and .server; BonjourBrowseTests, BonjourPipesTests, LanResolveTests, ConnectLanTests.

connect.relay.note: client.connect.relayTicket() and PolarisKey ConnectRelay (URLSessionWebSocketTask with the pkey-relay.1 subprotocol and the ticket, reconnect policy, LIMIT and close codes 4001/4003/4008/4009, mode-a relay sessions, pacing, 8 MiB outbox cap with per-session accounting); ConnectRelayTests, ConnectRelaySessionTests, ConnectRelayTicketTests; TranscriptTests replays connect-relay-ticket and connect-relay-quota.

connect.links.note: client.cloudConnect.links (sdks/swift/Sources/PolarisKey/CloudLinks.swift, CC-19.7; WIRE-CONTRACT-V5 section 15.10): pair(LinkPairOptions) opens the pairing window (ConnectLinkPairing.swift: an m=p advert with a random instance and the product tag, a listener of its own, at most 300 s; the lower instance dials; mode p to the code with PeerChannel's contact exchange, then the store), list(), remove(id) (the secret leaves the record, open sessions hear peer_revoked), setReachable(id, on), open(id) (mode c over the LAN, then the contact relay: ConnectContactRelay.swift opens a room per contact with the {room:"c", rid} ticket and speaks aliases only), onLink(fn) and interAccount(). The contacts are rows of the Connect record (ConnectState.swift, one Keychain item, wiped by leave(); a bad row makes the record unreadable); the shared LAN listener tries the account keys, then the contact secrets in trial order under one HandshakeLimiter; m=c adverts (at most 8, registered with DNS-SD beside the listener's account advert: BonjourContactAdverts.swift) and browse use PeerContacts.instance and a per-epoch name index; a pending contact is promoted by the first handshake that passes the pin. Everything is gated on the cached discovery interAccount (CloudLinksDisabled, code connect_links_disabled, otherwise). PeerContactTests.swift (@pkey-feature connect.links) runs the peer-matrix contact rows and two real channels; ConnectLinksTests.swift runs two accounts over the LAN and through a contact room; the connect-relay-ticket-contact and connect-links-disabled transcripts replay in TranscriptTests.swift. Secrets: Data is copy-on-write and CryptoKit copies its inputs, so a secret cannot be zeroed once it is in HKDF or HMAC; the copies this SDK owns are released, not overwritten. BonjourContactAdvertsTests.swift (CC-19.POLISH) keeps a registration by name and port; a contact row's categories must match ^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$.

connect.transfer.note: client.cloudConnect.transfer (sdks/swift/Sources/PolarisKey/CloudTransfer.swift, CC-20.6; WIRE-CONTRACT-V5 section 15.11): send(peer, source:, options:) (a device or a link; a file, Data or an AsyncThrowingStream spooled and hashed first), send(over:), onOffer(handler) (consent per transfer: .decline or .accept(to:); no handler declines; a mode-c offer is judged against the link's categories first), onReceived, cancel(id) and setMaxSize. The machine is PolarisKeyCore PeerXfer.swift (codecs, window, offer order, hash, ending, resume, limits, the partial path and the display-name cleaner), PeerXferEndpoint.swift runs it over a session, PeerXferStore.swift keeps the partial files (state/xfer, owner-only, named only by the derived path, delivery by link or copy through a temporary file and never over an existing file). PeerChannel owns the six record types when both payloads list xfer/1 (attachXfer, sendXfer; MORE is peer_bad_frame, no capability is peer_not_allowed, sendRecord refuses them); the LAN, relay and contact channels list xfer/1 by default. Each session owns the partials it claims (a second session of the same peer cannot touch them, a closed session's late effects are dropped, a purge of the peer refuses what is queued), and an accepted transfer reserves its declared size against the store quota (4 GiB) and the disk reserve (256 MiB) until it ends, writes past it are refused, a resume whose partial is gone or short starts at 0, and an effect queued before a purge is refused. Sign-out deletes every partial file; removing a link or a device leaving the roster deletes that peer's. PeerXferTests.swift replays every xfer row of peer-matrix.json (@pkey-feature connect.transfer); TransferTests.swift runs two in-process sessions (offer, accept, deliver; decline; consent timeout; cancel on either side; resume after a dropped session; hash mismatch; path-shaped names; the store).
